\paragraph{What we do not establish, in plain terms.}

\noindent\textbf{What the accuracy aggregates}: \textbf{a heterogeneous mixture}---instruction-following (equalization takes 97.0\% to 43.3\%), surface correction markers (a parameter-free 14-pattern rule reaches 69--80\% with nothing fit), a component \emph{consistent with} knowledge conflict (70.0\% KNOWN vs.\ 57.6\% UNKNOWN, $p\!=\!0.0045$, stratified observational), and \emph{sometimes} deception-associated behavior (one of five targets, at byte-identical elicitation)---\textbf{and once the instruction confound is removed, what remains is neither stable across targets nor cleanly separable from surface behavior} (§\ref{sec:experiments}, §\ref{sec:external_audit}). Criteria~1--4 test these one at a time (Table~\ref{tab:criteria}); no one of them by itself is deception detection, and an accuracy figure does not say which it is measuring.

\paragraph{Panel-level outcomes (PREREG~§5, §6).}
Across the 7 targets the parameter-free rule spans \textbf{80.0--90.0\%} and the transferred pipeline \textbf{40.0--56.0\%}. At $n\!=\!100$ the smallest count significantly above chance is 61/100, so every rule cell clears that floor, and no pipeline cell reaches it, making the split between the two outcomes complete across the panel.

\textbf{H1} (exact two-sided binomial, Holm-corrected within the 5 new targets, within each outcome family separately): the rule is above chance on \textbf{5 of 5} new targets (largest $p_{\mathrm{Holm}}\!<\!0.001$), the pipeline on \textbf{0 of 5} (smallest $p_{\mathrm{Holm}}\!=\!0.284$). Cells between 40\% and 61\% are reported as \emph{not distinguishable from chance at $n\!=\!100$}, never as ``at chance'' (PREREG~§6).

\textbf{H2} (homogeneity of proportions; the version over the new targets alone is the one carrying confirmatory weight, PREREG~§0) --- rule, all 7: $\chi^2\!=\!6.33$, $\mathrm{df}\!=\!6$, $p\!=\!0.387$; rule, 5 new: $\chi^2\!=\!5.48$, $\mathrm{df}\!=\!4$, $p\!=\!0.241$; pipeline, all 7: $\chi^2\!=\!5.98$, $\mathrm{df}\!=\!6$, $p\!=\!0.426$; pipeline, 5 new: $\chi^2\!=\!5.37$, $\mathrm{df}\!=\!4$, $p\!=\!0.252$. No test departs from a common rate, so the panel gives no evidence that these targets differ from one another on either outcome.

\textbf{H3} (closed- versus open-weight, \textbf{descriptive only}) --- rule 164/199 closed vs.\ 437/500 open ($-5.0$\,pp, Fisher exact $p\!=\!0.0918$); pipeline 106/199 vs.\ 229/500 ($+7.5$\,pp, $p\!=\!0.0786$). \textbf{We make no attribution to weight availability.} The pairwise two-proportion MDE at $n\!=\!100$ per cell is 19.4\,pp, ``closed'' is 2 \emph{organizations}, and weight availability, architecture, RLHF recipe and serving stack remain collinear at the panel level (PREREG~§6, §11).

\paragraph{The Anthropic row's two extractor arms (PREREG~§4).}
Claude Haiku~4.5 extracts features for all 7 targets, so for the Anthropic target alone the extractor is \emph{same-family}. The pre-registration therefore makes the cross-family extractor (Llama-3.3-70B) \textbf{primary} for that row and Haiku the sensitivity arm, and requires both to be reported and never averaged. The transferred pipeline reaches \textbf{49.5\%} (48/97) under the primary arm and 50.5\% (50/99) under the sensitivity arm---1.0\,pp apart, both degenerate (every trial predicted truthful) and both below the 61/100 floor, so which arm is read does not change this row's verdict. The table prints the same-family value, which is the published one. \textbf{How the primary arm was obtained, since it is not a second run:} its committed file re-extracts features with the cross-family extractor but stores the same-family run's detector outputs verbatim, so the classifier was replayed offline over the committed feature trajectories---with no model calls, and only after that replay reproduced the same-family arm's stored confidences, stopping points and predictions bit for bit. The 2 trials whose re-extraction failed at or after the deciding step are excluded and not imputed. The parameter-free rule cannot differ between the arms at all: it reads the target's own turns, which both files share.

The two cells therefore do not constitute a mechanistic double dissociation. \textbf{The confound this design named is now broken}: EXP-FS adds five further targets from five further organizations---including DeepSeek-V3, one of the two this sentence named as an example before any of them was run---so closed/open weight, dense/MoE architecture and RLHF recipe are no longer collinear across the panel (Table~\ref{tab:frontier_panel}).

\textbf{We do not establish that the collapse reproduces on current-generation models}, and nothing here should be read as evidence that it does or does not. The prediction is sharp, and we attempted to falsify it: \textbf{EXP-R1d (Appendix~\ref{app:r1d}) ran it on four current-generation targets and is \emph{inconclusive}}---three void on a pre-registered probe-channel gate, one admissible target falling $-46.0$\,pp---which is why the sentence above stands unchanged rather than being replaced by a result.

\textbf{The trained-pipeline collapse now has a current-generation test, and it survives it.} The pre-registered frontier panel (Appendix~\ref{app:frontier_panel}) transfers the trained detector unchanged onto 7 frontier-scale targets from 7 organizations under a byte-identical neutral prompt, and every cell lands at 40.0--56.0\%---below the 61/100 count that would be significant at $n\!=\!100$. No test departs from a common rate across the panel, so \textbf{the pipeline collapse of §\ref{sec:prompt_equalized} is not specific to the $\leq$70B open-weight vintage we measured it on} (PREREG~§7, Branch~A). \textbf{Two things this does not give us.} It is \emph{not} a current-generation test of EXP-R1c's 16-probe battery, a different detector that was not run on these targets; there the recency question stays open, and our attempt on it (Appendix~\ref{app:r1d}) is \emph{inconclusive}---three targets void on a pre-registered probe-channel gate, one admissible target falling $-46.0$\,pp. And it runs the \emph{other} way for the surface rule: the parameter-free 14-pattern rule reaches 80.0--90.0\% across the same panel, \textbf{above} its 69--80\% range on the $\leq$70B roster, so \textbf{surface-accessible accuracy does not collapse at frontier scale} and is the more robust of the two findings---an emphasis shift the pre-registration committed to in advance (PREREG~§8.2).
